primitives.name: Schema-First Evidence
primitives.assumptions: Assumes a well-defined data contract exists in the form of a JSON schema, and that this contract is the single source of truth for data validation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the schema evolves faster than the ability to update dependent systems, leading to version conflicts.

layer2.mapping: The schema acts as a conformal prediction region for data points; violations indicate distribution shift. In GSI, it maps to evidence contracts that guarantee data integrity for betting models. In GSE, it underpins situational awareness by ensuring consistent state transitions across microservices.
layer2.telemetry: Proportion of data records failing schema validation, monitored over time.

primitives.name: Local Model Card
primitives.verbatim_quote: Registry | markdown/model-card fixture | model governance | future fixture test | | drift bucket replay
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that model performance metrics can be summarized in a reproducible, human-readable document.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the card becomes a static artifact rather than an evolving record of model behavior.

layer2.mapping: The model card provides a deterministic summary of a model's behavior, analogous to a GSI calibration report. In GSE, it serves as a local fixture for testing model governance policies during state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Card generation success rate and update frequency.

primitives.name: Drift Bucket Replay
primitives.verbatim_quote: Model Monitor | local drift checks | calibration monitoring | drift tests | | explainability notes
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that statistical drift between training and serving data can be detected using historical buckets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when the drift signal is confounded by noise or when the bucket size is too small to capture true shifts.

layer2.mapping: Replaying past drift buckets simulates retroactive calibration adjustments. In GSI, it maps to conformal prediction intervals that adapt to covariate shift. In GSE, it enables state-transition testing under distributional perturbations.
layer2.telemetry: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) on drifted test sets.

primitives.name: Explainability Notes
primitives.verbatim_quote: Clarify | parity and segment docs | bias/fairness review | parity tests | | agent tool
primitives.assumptions: Assumes that model explanations can be systematically documented and verified against fairness criteria.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when explanations are insufficiently detailed to diagnose specific sources of bias.

layer2.mapping: Explanations provide a discrete partition of feature space, similar to GSI parity analysis. In GSE, they inform safety constraints during state transitions, ensuring that agent actions remain within safe operational regions.
layer2.telemetry: Number of identified bias sources per model release.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is managing uncertainty in data and model behavior while avoiding unnecessary costs. These primitives form a cascading pipeline: a schema ensures data consistency, model cards provide interpretability, drift detection monitors for distributional shifts, and explainability pinpoints sources of bias. Each step introduces a duality: the tension between automation (reliability) and manual oversight (accountability). The failure mode occurs when any link breaks, causing downstream errors. For instance, a relaxed schema might allow corrupted data into the system, undermining all subsequent checks. To prevent this, we impose a "cost cap gate" that limits resource consumption, creating a feedback loop that enforces fiscal discipline. This framework aligns with the broader goal of building trustworthy AI: it provides empirical verifiable artifacts that map directly to both GSI's probabilistic forecasts and GSE's dynamic decision-making.
